name: CR-Int-15-partialfrac-9
questiontext:
Write \[ {{CT:0}}\] as partial fractions.

[[input:ap]].
[[validation:ap]]
[[feedback:partfrac]]

Find \[ \int {{CT:0}} d{{CT:1}}. \]

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
[[feedback:Result]]
generalfeedback:
Since the degree of the numerator equal to the degree of the denominator we need to use long division.
\[{{CT:0}} = {{CT:2}} + {{CT:3}}.\]
Hence, using partial fractions we have
\[{{CT:0}} = {{CT:4}}.\]

So,
\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 \int {{CT:0}} d{{CT:1}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \int {{CT:4}} d{{CT:1}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:5}} \int {{CT:6}} d{{CT:1}} + {{CT:7}} \int {{CT:8}} d{{CT:1}} + {{CT:9}} \int \left({{CT:10}}\right) d{{CT:1}} + \int {{CT:3}} d{{CT:1}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:11}} + {{CT:12}} + {{CT:13}}+ {{CT:14}} + c \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:15}}+c
 \end{array}\]
